note: Read 2026-10-31 in the Immigration and Refugee Board of Canada's response to information request DJI105551.FE (covering 2014 to July 2016), as ecoi.net hosts it. It quotes the EU's PRADO register (its Djibouti licence entry, which answers this egress with a browser check): category B from 18, of indefinite validity (A1 from 16, C 5 years, D 2 or 1 years); a representative of Djibouti's embassy in Washington, in writing on 29 June 2016: the Ministry of the Interior issues driving licences, only in Djibouti, and the licence has unlimited validity; a Djibouti lawyer adds that the Service des mines under the Ministry issues them. The report also quotes a study of the Institut supérieur des affaires de Djibouti (on the Ministry of Economy and Finance's site) listing B at 18 and a file with two 500 DJF fiscal stamps and 7,000 DJF paid at the District; that study isn't an official tariff, so the fee is null. The sources are of 2016 or undated: no later text of Djibouti's own was found (transports.gouv.dj gave no answer today; the presidency's site held no licence text when tried on 30 October), so that the rule still holds rests on them.

sources.title: Djibouti: Driver's licences, including the authorities that issue them, their validity period, and the requirements and procedure for obtaining one (2014-July 2016), DJI105551.FE, Immigration and Refugee Board of Canada (ecoi.net)
